- When sentiment shows strong positive change followed by a spike, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative or flat over 3+ days, model overcorrects downward — adjust downward bias by +2–5% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- High news volume with low sentiment change suggests market noise — dampen forecast volatility by 10–20%.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often lags — forecast should be adjusted up by 1–3% on the first day of sentiment shift.
- If true outcome shows sharp upward trend after model overestimates, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 2–3 days to avoid overhang.
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overpredicts by >5% in early days, reduce early forecast by 2–4% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
